name: Chamfer & Fillet Guide
blurb: recommended chamfers and radii by manufacturing process
intro: Which edges to chamfer, which corners to round, and by how much, for the process that makes the part. Values follow published design guides (Covestro/Bayer, NADCA, ISO 13715, CNC and printing service guides); rules that scale with wall thickness or pocket depth are computed from your numbers.

inputs.label: Wall / sheet thickness
inputs.help: Nominal wall for moulding, casting and printing; sheet thickness for sheet metal.

inputs.label: Pocket depth
inputs.help: Deepest pocket with inside corners (CNC milling).

examples.title: Milled aluminium housing, 18 mm deep pockets

usage: Give process (mill, turn, fdm, sla, sls, mold, diecast, sheet or all), the wall or sheet thickness t in mm and, for milling, the deepest pocket depth in mm; filter narrows the rows by words. It returns the key recommended radii/chamfers as values and a table of feature, recommended and minimum size, the rule and why. Use it when modelling edges and corners so the part suits its process.
sources: Covestro (Bayer) 'Engineering Polymers: Part and Mold Design', corners and ribs (R_in = 0.5 t, R_out = 1.5 t)
NADCA Product Specification Standards for Die Castings, section 4A (fillets and radii)
ISO 13715 edges of undefined shape (edge break 0.2-0.5 mm)
Hubs / Protolabs CNC machining design guides (internal corner R >= depth/3)
Rule of thumb for printing values (FDM/SLA/SLS vendor design guides)
